extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

faqs.q: What is the Drill String Compensator Hose used for?
faqs.a: The Drill String Compensator Hose is used for active heave compensation of the drill string on an offshore rig. It is a tensioner compensator hose in 2" to 4" bore, rated 5000 psi WP, 12500 psi MBP, from the Continental range.

faqs.q: What do WP and MBP mean in the 5000 psi WP, 12500 psi MBP rating of the Drill String Compensator Hose?
faqs.a: WP is the working pressure, the continuous service rating, and MBP is the minimum burst pressure, a design margin and never a working pressure. The Drill String Compensator Hose is rated 5000 psi WP, 12500 psi MBP. The hydrotest is 1.5 times working pressure per the listing.

faqs.q: What bore sizes does the Drill String Compensator Hose come in?
faqs.a: The listing gives 2" to 4" inside diameter for the Drill String Compensator Hose, with flanged end fittings. Sizes outside the range can be quoted with a longer lead time. Give the inside diameter and assembly length on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Should I choose the Drill String Compensator Hose or the Riser Tensioner Hose?
faqs.a: The drill string compensator hose serves the compensator that holds weight on bit as the rig heaves, while a riser tensioner hose serves the tensioner that supports the marine riser. See the [Riser Tensioner Hose](/p/riser-tensioner-hose).

faqs.q: What is the temperature range of the Drill String Compensator Hose?
faqs.a: The listing gives -30°C to +82°C for the Drill String Compensator Hose. Sour-service and high-temperature variants exist for most families, so give the wellbore conditions on the RFQ for an engineering review.

faqs.q: What are the liner and reinforcement of the Drill String Compensator Hose?
faqs.a: The liner is Hydraulic-fluid-compatible synthetic rubber and the reinforcement is multiple high-tensile steel cable plies — heavy-cycle-rated. The flanged couplings are fitted to suit the Drill String Compensator Hose. Match the liner to the fluid, because the liner decides chemical resistance.

faqs.q: Which API standard does the Drill String Compensator Hose meet, and is it API monogrammed?
faqs.a: The listing gives API Spec 7K for the Drill String Compensator Hose. It is supplied by API-licensed manufacturers to API 7K with the API certificate and monogram documentation issued with the order, and a test certificate with each assembly. Read the [API 7K, 16C and 16D guide](/blog/api-7k-16c-16d-which-standard).

faqs.q: What end fittings does the Drill String Compensator Hose use?
faqs.a: The Drill String Compensator Hose uses flanged end fittings. Flanges are API 6A or API 6BX, raised-face or ring-joint, so state the flange size, pressure class and gasket type on the RFQ; ring gaskets are in the [ring joint gasket range](/c/ring-joint-gaskets). See the [oilfield hose guide](/blog/oilfield-hose-guide).

faqs.q: How should I inspect and replace the Drill String Compensator Hose?
faqs.a: Inspect the Drill String Compensator Hose for cover damage, kinks, leaks and end-fitting movement at each rig move or as your procedure requires, and retire it per the maker's guidance and your records. Plan replacements around permits; see the [rig-site hose replacement guide](/blog/rig-site-hose-replacement-abu-dhabi) and the [guide for this hose type](/blog/riser-tensioner-and-compensator-hose).
